messages:
marta: Heads up — seeing a cluster of Xid 13 and 31 on several A10 cards in us-east1 during overnight small-batch embed jobs. Suspect decode/embed overlap on low-latency parallel requests. Sample dmesg from gpu-7:
```
[12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=1423, GPU=7
[12345.679100] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=1423, GPU=7
[12345.679350] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=1424, GPU=7
```

devin: Ugh. Any tenant/job correlation? op-type breakdown? :thinking_face:

sidharth: I pulled the optype heatmap for last 6 hrs — ~88% embeddings (small batches, seq len ~64), occasional decode spikes when customers call streaming. Xid 31 seems to align with a specific tenant's bursty embed traffic.

linh: Which tenant? can we repro in a dev pool?

marta: tenant-42 shows repeated failures. Jobs: embed-2026-03-17-22* (short ids). Repro is possible with our embed micro-benchmark (batch sizes 1-4, concurrency 60).

carlos: Quick triage notes: Xid 13 often = illegal memory access (could be driver or bad kernel module), Xid 31 tends to be page fault/firmware-related. Both on same card suggests either intermittent HW or driver/stack bug triggered by this workload mix.

marta: ops-bot started a soft-drain on gpu-7 to stop new allocations while we triage. :robot_face:

ops-bot: Soft-drain initiated on node gpu-7 by marta at 2026-03-17T05:46:40Z. Current tasks will be allowed to finish.

devin: Can someone grab full kernel logs + nvidia-smi -q around the failures? Also check ECC counters. If ECC spikes it points to HW.

sidharth: Attached quick ECC snapshot: no ECC correctable/unrecoverable spikes across the board. Memory errors are flat. That makes me lean toward driver/kernel issue or a bad firmware race under small-batch concurrency.

marta: Collected logs and core dumps (uploaded to /mnt/ci/triage/2315/). Key snippets: journalctl shows NVRM Xid entries, dmesg matches. Also saw a few `gpu-reset` events on same node.

linh: Steps I propose:
1) repro in dev pool with same concurrency/batch patterns (sidharth)
2) test on same host with stock driver vs pinned older driver (marta)
3) run GPU memtest (carlos)
4) if repro fails on driver older/newer -> open NVIDIA SR with logs (devin)

carlos: I can run memtest tonight. If memtest finds WR/rd errors -> replace card. If memtest clean and repro deterministic by workload -> escalate to NVIDIA.

devin: Also worth enabling per-tenant routing to fallback to different instance types as temporary mitigation (route tenant-42 to E4 instead of A10 in us-east1) to avoid user impact while we triage.

marta: Created a short-lived route for tenant-42 to eu-west fallback and scaled capacity to avoid throttles. Observed almost zero Xid after routing them off the affected hosts (so far).

sidharth: I'll run the micro-bench with stress patterns (burstiness + mixed decode/embed) on a reserved A10 in staging and collect nvbug traces. Will post results by EOD.

carlos: Commands I used / recommend for quick checks:
```bash
sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,compute_mode,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
journalctl -k | grep -i nvrm | tail -n 200
sudo cat /sys/class/drm/card*/device/uevent
# memtest (from diagnostics image): /opt/gpu-tools/gpu_memtest --pass 3
```

marta: Action items:
- marta: collect full nvlogs + upload (done)
- sidharth: repro + nvbug traces in staging (in progress)
- carlos: memtest on gpu-7 hardware (scheduled)
- devin: prepare SR with NVIDIA if repro + logs point to driver/firmware (standby)

linh: If memtest clean and SR opened, ask NVIDIA to look specifically at concurrent small-batch embed path + seq len ~64 + concurrency ~60 — we saw the failure surface there.

marta: Noted. Will also tag related dashboards and add a short postmortem stub if we have a replacement or driver SR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

devin: FYI I bumped monitoring alert threshold so we get an incident channel if Xid > 3 on any node within 30m window.

ops-bot: Ticket INF-1629 created to track triage steps. Linked: https://redwood.internal/infra/tickets/INF-1629

marta: Closing loop — will update here after memtest and staging repro.
